paper_id: Liu et al. - 2012 - Mining Frequent Trajectory Patterns for Activity Monitoring Using Radio Frequency Tag Arrays
title: Mining Frequent Trajectory Patterns for Activity Monitoring Using Radio Frequency Tag Arrays
venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems
motivation: 视频监控成本高覆盖有限,RFID阵列提供经济方案
problem_framing: 从有噪声的RF标签信号序列中挖掘频繁轨迹模式
key_insight: 利用物体穿过标签阵列时的信号干扰变化检测轨迹,无需在被追踪对象上安装设备
evaluation_criteria: 正确检测轨迹长度与实际路线长度之比
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: min_sup=3时准确率降至60%;时间间隔小于20秒的多目标难以区分;复杂活动仍有挑战
evidence_for_taste: the normal trajectories of moving objects often follow regular patterns
All the previous proposals assumed the data are precise, therefore, they cannot be applied
the probability is unknown and hard to be estimated. Thus, the property has to be used as a heuristic
Such situations can hardly be handled well by video monitoring systems either
thinking_moves: 把感知问题重新定义为数据挖掘问题
用Chebyshev不等式证明检测阈值
用边界检测消除冗余信息
深度优先搜索扩展频繁段,近者优先扩展以剪枝
跨读卡器交叉验证消除冗余模式
cites_own_work: RASS: A Real-Time, Accurate and Scalable System for Tracking Transceiver-Free Objects
TASA: Tag-Free Activity Sensing Using RFID Tag Arrays
